note: The club operated from February 1900 until October 1911, owned by Ada and Minna Everleigh (born Simms in Greene County, Virginia, 1864 and 1866; the Kentucky childhood was 'another story concocted by the sisters'); they bought Effie Hankins's brothel at 2131-2133 South Dearborn; it had 'a $15,000 gold-leafed piano for the Music Room' and '$650 gold cuspidors'; it 'opened on February 1, 1900'; Ada kept the books and hired, Minna met the guests; Prince Henry of Prussia visited on 3 March 1902 and the slipper-champagne story began there; the club employed '15 to 25 cooks and maids'. Mayor Carter Harrison Jr. ordered it closed on 24 October 1911; Minna: 'If the Mayor says we must close, that settles it...I'll close up shop and walk out with a smile on my face.' The building was razed in July 1933. On 22 November 1905 Marshall Field Jr. was shot; 'there is some evidence that he was shot by a prostitute at the Everleigh Club', and 'A rival madam maliciously accused the Everleigh sisters of murdering Field.'
